name: A01: Broken Access Control
evidence: Authenticated resource-scoped routes with ID parameters exist, including users, cards, addresses, baskets, and other objects.

name: A02: Cryptographic Failures
evidence: The application includes password handling, JWT authentication, 2FA, cryptographic key-serving routes, and encryption-related dependencies.

name: A03: Injection
evidence: The architecture reports no raw SQL queries, no raw-query files, and no MongoDB/NoSQL usage or explicit eval/exec mechanisms.

name: A04: Insecure Design
evidence: The architecture exposes many sensitive business flows and intentionally insecure challenge routes, but design-level weaknesses cannot be reliably determined from route inventory alone.

name: A05: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: XML parsing, YAML parsing, CORS, static file serving, directory indexes, public metrics, and multiple unauthenticated sensitive-looking surfaces are present.

name: A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
evidence: The application has 117 dependencies, including security-relevant components such as old JWT, Helmet, js-yaml, multer, and sanitize-html packages.

name: A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
evidence: Login, password change/reset, security-question, JWT authentication, 2FA, and rate-limited authentication endpoints are present.

name: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
evidence: The application processes uploaded YAML/XML/ZIP files, handles webhooks, performs data restoration, and exposes deserialization-like file-processing flows.

name: A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
evidence: A logging module, log-serving routes, metrics middleware, and public metrics endpoints are present.

name: A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
evidence: A profile image URL upload route and corresponding profileImageUrlUpload handler indicate server-side retrieval of user-supplied URLs.

name: API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
evidence: The REST/API surface contains numerous ID-based object routes, including users, baskets, cards, addresses, reviews, and orders.

name: API2: Broken Authentication
evidence: The API exposes login, password reset, JWT-based authorization, 2FA verification, and authenticated user flows.

name: API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
evidence: Twenty-eight auto-CRUD routes expose model properties, with only limited exclusions such as password and totpSecret on User.

name: API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
evidence: The API includes file uploads, pagination-enabled auto-CRUD, data export, AI chat, Web3 operations, and many endpoints without visible rate limiting.

name: API5: Broken Function Level Authorization
evidence: The API contains administrative, accounting, product, user, order, wallet, and challenge functions with varied or absent authorization middleware.

name: API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
evidence: Sensitive flows include registration, password reset, checkout, coupon application, wallet funding, deluxe membership, data export, and order tracking.

name: API7: Server Side Request Forgery
evidence: The profile image URL upload functionality provides an apparent server-side URL-fetching capability.

name: API8: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: Only one Swagger path is documented while 109 hand-written and 28 auto-CRUD routes are undocumented; numerous public static and operational surfaces also exist.

name: API9: Improper Inventory Management
evidence: The architecture explicitly identifies 109 undocumented hand-written routes and 28 undocumented auto-CRUD routes.

name: API10: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
evidence: The application integrates OpenAI-compatible AI services, Web3/blockchain functionality, webhooks, and URL-based resource retrieval.

name: LLM01: Prompt Injection
evidence: A chat endpoint uses an LLM with user-provided conversational input and tool-calling enabled.

name: LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure
evidence: LLM tools can query products, reviews, and orders and perform authenticated database operations, creating a data-disclosure capability.

name: LLM03: Supply Chain
evidence: The application depends on AI SDK and OpenAI-compatible provider components and delegates tool-enabled behavior to external model infrastructure.

name: LLM05: Improper Output Handling
evidence: LLM responses and tool results are consumed by the chat frontend, but the architecture does not establish whether output validation, encoding, or authorization checks are inadequate.

name: LLM06: Excessive Agency
evidence: The LLM can invoke executable tools that query data, perform authentication-aware operations, retrieve orders, and generate coupons.

name: LLM10: Unbounded Consumption
evidence: A public chat endpoint enables LLM interaction and tool invocation, while no dedicated chat/LLM rate limit or token/resource bound is shown.
